_meta.purpose: Replacements for claims in data/eras/*.json whose only inline cite is Wikipedia (WP:* ids or registry ids whose url is wikipedia.org). Modern eras (start >= 1956) are listed first. Every replacement was read in full on 2026-10-25. Nothing in data/ was edited; the Historian applies the changes.
_meta.method: Every *_en string in data/eras/*.json was split into sentences, and the cite ids were collected (registry ids in parentheses plus bare WP:* tokens). A sentence was kept when all of its ids are Wikipedia. Result: 3 claims in 2 eras. Arabic fields mirror the English ones and need the same cite change. Re-scan on 2026-10-25 found a 4th claim (al-bashir economy_en, DE_WIKI_HIST).
_meta.war_control_claims: None of the 3 claims is a war-control claim, so nothing is marked CUT.

replacement.citation: Satti, Noureddine. Chapter 'Le Soudan aujourd'hui' (section 'Islamisme et politique au Soudan'), in Histoire et civilisations du Soudan. Soleb / Bleu autour / SFDAS, 2017.
replacement.quote: Jusqu’au coup d’État de juin 1989 qui a amené au pouvoir le régime islamiste du colonel Omar Hassan Ahmed el-Bechir. [...] L’islamisme soudanais ne fait pas exception : son objectif ultime est l’islamisation de la société par des moyens musclés

claims.note: The source dates the regime's Islamisation aim from the June 1989 coup. It does not say 'early 1990s'. The Historian should either match the text to the source or keep the wording and add [SINGLE-SOURCE]. I have not reworded anything.

claims.claim: sharia applied in the North only under the CPA (FR_WIKI_HIST)

replacement.citation: The Comprehensive Peace Agreement between the Government of the Republic of the Sudan and the SPLM/SPLA (2005), Chapter I: The Machakos Protocol, s. 3.2.2.
replacement.quote: Nationally enacted legislation having effect only in respect of the states outside Southern Sudan shall have as its source of legislation Sharia and the consensus of the people.

claims.note: Primary treaty text, 261 pp, downloaded and text-extracted in full on 2026-10-25. The UN Peacemaker copy returns 404, so I used the UCDP copy, which is the URL already in the registry.

claims.claim: investment came from China, Malaysia and India (DE_WIKI_HIST).

replacement.citation: Patey, Luke Anthony. 'State rules: Oil companies and armed conflict in Sudan', Third World Quarterly 28:5 (2007), 997-1016. DOI 10.1080/01436590701371728.
replacement.quote: State- owned oil companies from China, Malaysia and India would dominate Sudan’s oil industry as the Western juniors pulled-out. Fittingly, it was China, with the most urgent energy demands, that moved first. In 1995 Beijing’s powerhouse oil company, CNPC, quietly bought the former Chevron concession

claims.note: Peer-reviewed article, 21-page PDF read in full on 2026-10-25. It covers the oil sector, not all investment; the Historian may want to narrow the wording. IMF CR 20/73 Selected Issues (oil sector) returned 403 to curl and timed out in WebFetch, so it was not used.

claims.claim: Colonial phase (Italian colony from 1890) not covered by a read source [thin; WP:Eritrea only].

replacement.citation: Eritrea-Ethiopia Boundary Commission, Decision regarding delimitation of the border between Eritrea and Ethiopia, 13 April 2002. UN Reports of International Arbitral Awards (RIAA) vol. XXV, pp. 83-195.
replacement.quote: On 1 January 1890, Italy formally established the Colony of Eritrea.

claims.note: This is not a modern era (it starts in 1890) and is listed after the modern ones. The registry title of EEBC2002 still carries [VERIFY]. I read the decision in full on 2026-10-25, so the Historian may drop that tag. The bracketed note '[thin; WP:Eritrea only]' would then be out of date; any rewording is the Historian's call.
